newsitem.title: USA: US Housing starts remain strong as economy expands.
newsitem.headline: US Housing starts remain strong as economy expands.

text.p: U.S. April housing starts came in higher than consensus expectations on Friday despite heavy flooding in portions of the Midwest.

Housing starts rose 2.6 percent to an annualized level of 1.47 million. Economists polled by Reuters had expected, on average, that starts would rise slightly to 1.43 million annualized from March's 1.425 million pace.
"It's in line with what we were looking for -- a bit above consensus -- following a pullback in March, said Kevin Flanagan, economist with Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.
